newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto's estranged sister-in-law sees tough fight.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's estranged sister-in-law sees tough fight.

text.p: The estranged sister-in-law of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Saturday she faced a tough fight in Pakistan's general elections on Monday but her faction would win many parliamentary seats.

The Lebanese-born Ghinwa is the widow of Bhutto's younger brother Murtaza, who was killed in a police shootout in Karachi last September, and now leads her husband's breakaway Shaheed Bhutto faction of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP).
"The tilt of the voters is towards us," she told Reuters before leaving for her last campaign rally in the nearby village of Dohri in the Bhutto family's home province of Sindh.
Ghinwa, who is a candidate against her Iranian-born mother-in-law Nusrat, patron of Bhutto's party, said her faction was strong in Sindh province.
"Floating votes are coming towards Murtaza's party, which stands for justice," she said.
Ghinwa supports the November 5 dismissal of Bhutto's three-year-old government by President Farooq Leghari on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Political sources say Ghinwa will cooperate with Bhutto's main rival, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, in forming the next government.
